arms.better: tm needs to stop repeated inspections sooner and turn its own recovery prompt into a focused action rather than rescheduling nearly identical investigations. Here it read src/requests/models.py repeatedly, consumed 139,430 reported tokens over three attempts, and ended with no patch; the messages asked the operator to continue saved sessions with tm --resume S-1/S-2/S-3 but did not recover automatically or summarize a concrete next change. A clear budget/progress message with a single useful finding and one bounded recovery attempt would have made the run easier to understand and less costly.

OpenCode could have avoided unnecessary test-writing and test-debugging context by using the issue's exact delegated-attribute wrapper and running the project's provided hidden regression test after completing the fix. Its first locally added test incorrectly passed BytesIO, which is already directly iterable; it then spent several turns chasing pytest importing Requests from another checkout. Despite this, it noticed and disclosed the wrong-source test run, and the protocol's authoritative hidden test passed after the arm's implementation was kept and the merged test file was checked out.
